items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: compared to Dizzy and Fats Navarro

ctx.x: They just would say, “Yeah, yeah, you’re doing good, keep it up,” and they were encouraging but not over the top.

Right. Well for example when Miles joined Charlie Parker, he could hardly play with them compared to Dizzy and Fats Navarro. As a trumpet player he was very weak. But I guess Bird saw something in his communication or the way his style was that he saw promise there. And that’s the other thing I cherish about the black cats that I owe my life to. They gave you a lot of headway. If they saw something that was good they allowed it to develop, rather than more like you know I hate to say this in the white world you…
As a young man going into these clubs and playing with these gentlemen, was there ever any uncomfortable situations as far as the racial end of things?
